mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x - x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mn>120</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mo>⋯</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{x^5}{120} - \cdots</annotation></semantics></math>: the leading term is negative.

Divide each term by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3</annotation></semantics></math> first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>120</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mo>⋯</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{6} + \frac{x^2}{120} - \cdots</annotation></semantics></math>, which approaches <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: For <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mo><</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|x| < 3</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(n + 1)x^n}{3^n}</annotation></semantics></math>. Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'''(0)</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{27}</annotation></semantics></math> is the coefficient of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3</annotation></semantics></math>, which equals <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f'''(0)}{3!}</annotation></semantics></math>. Multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3! = 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies the coefficient <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4}{27}</annotation></semantics></math> by 3. Multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>!</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3! = 6</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">‴</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>4</mn><mn>27</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>8</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f'''(0) = 6 \cdot \frac{4}{27} = \frac{8}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Write the first four nonzero terms of the Maclaurin series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Substitute <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = -x^2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^2 = x^4</annotation></semantics></math> but <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = -x^2</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>u</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u^3 = -x^6</annotation></semantics></math>, so the signs alternate.

Substitute <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x^2</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-x</annotation></semantics></math>: the powers are <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2, x^4, x^6</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: What is the radius of convergence of the series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>?

items.q: Integrate term by term from <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>: write the first four nonzero terms of the Maclaurin series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Integrating <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{2n}</annotation></semantics></math> gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{t^{2n+1}}{2n + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>: divide by the new power.

That differentiates the series; <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan x</annotation></semantics></math> is the integral of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + x^2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use the first two nonzero terms of the series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan x</annotation></semantics></math> to estimate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is only the first term; subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1/2)^3}{3} = \frac{1}{24}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The second term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1/2)^3}{3} = \frac{1}{24}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The series for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\arctan\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> alternates and its terms decrease in size to 0. mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{24}</annotation></semantics></math> is the last term used; the bound is the first term left out, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1/2)^5}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide by 5 as well: the term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>160</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1/2)^5}{5} = \frac{1}{160}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{1}{1 - x}\right)</annotation></semantics></math>, the sum of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mi>n</mi><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n x^{n-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, as an expression in <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The chain rule gives <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-(1 - x)^{-2} \cdot (-1)</annotation></semantics></math>: the two negatives cancel.

That is the original function; differentiate it: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}(1 - x)^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (1 - x)^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use the table to find the sum <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><mi>n</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{n}{2^n}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>n</mi><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum n\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>, but <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>n</mi><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{n}{2^n}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mi>n</mi><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{2} \cdot n\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{n-1}</annotation></semantics></math>: multiply by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

1 is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n</annotation></semantics></math>, the series without the factor <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the derivative series: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{(1 - 1/2)^2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Give the interval of convergence of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln(1 + x)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><munderover><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></munderover><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{n+1} x^n}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>.

ends.lo: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -1</annotation></semantics></math> every term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>n</mi></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(-1)^{n+1}(-1)^n}{n}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -\frac{1}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>: the negative of the harmonic series, which diverges.
ends.hi: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> the series is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}</annotation></semantics></math>, the alternating harmonic series, which converges.
